Projects and resources grouped by provider, for the DDI service.
Synchronisation details for a LEXIS Provider: users and their project roles.

get.description: Returns the project details for the specified short name.

put.description: Updates a project's name, description, contact email, validity period and domain type. The short name is immutable.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the project and cascade soft-deletes all project role rows. Returns 204; 404 out of scope / not found; 409 when the project is read-only.

get.description: Returns projects the authenticated user has a role on, optionally filtered by short name, contact email, domain type, and validity dates. startDate and endDate are ISO-8601 timestamps and bound the project's own validity period inclusively: startDate keeps projects whose StartDate is on or after it, endDate keeps projects whose EndDate is on or before it.

post.description: Creates a project and grants the creator the project owner role. Body {ShortName, Name, Description?, ContactEmail?, StartDate, EndDate, DomainTypeName}. Returns 201; 400 on validation / unknown domain type; 409 (code project.short_name_already_exists) when the short name already exists. Errors carry a machine-readable code in the problem extensions — branch on that, not the message.

get.summary: List users assigned to a project
get.description: Returns active users assigned to the specified project, with their project role, as a paged list (?page=&limit=). Errors carry a machine-readable code in the problem extensions — branch on that, not the message.
Returns a project with its full resource assignment and location allocation details. Each assigned resource carries its location's LocationType as a name.

Returns available HEAppE cluster and command template data for the project as a single complete page (bounded reference list — paging parameters are ignored). Requires X-Original-Authorization header (Keycloak bearer token).

post.summary: Create a tag and assign it to a project
post.description: Creates the named tag in the shared catalogue if it does not yet exist and assigns it to the project. Idempotent. Requires the tag-create permission.

put.summary: Assign an existing tag to a project
put.description: Associates an existing catalogue tag with the project. Returns 404 when no tag with that name exists; it never creates one (use POST to create). Idempotent. Tags are identified by name.

delete.summary: Remove a tag from a project
delete.description: Removes the named tag's association with the project. Idempotent. The shared tag itself is not deleted.

put.summary: Assign a user to a project
put.description: Assigns a user to the project as a project member (creates or reactivates the membership and the project role). Idempotent reactivation of a previously removed user. Returns 409 when the user is already an active member, or when the project is read-only.

delete.summary: Remove a user from a project
delete.description: Removes a user's membership and project role from the project. The project owner cannot be removed (409). Returns 404 when the user is not an active member, 409 when the project is read-only.

get.summary: List assignable project roles for the caller
get.description: Returns the project roles the caller may assign to other members of the project (strictly below the caller's own level, no lower than the member baseline) as a single complete page (bounded reference list — paging parameters are ignored).

put.description: Changes a member's project role; the target role name is supplied in the request body (Body {RoleName}, matched case-insensitively). The caller may only assign a role strictly below their own level and no lower than the member baseline (403 otherwise); a project may hold at most one owner (409). Returns 400 for an unknown role, 409 when the project is read-only.

get.description: Returns the provider details for the specified provider name.

Returns providers, optionally filtered by name and country. Paged via ?page=&limit= (default 50, max 200); the response body is the bare array, with pagination in the X-Total-Count and Link response headers.

[DEPRECATED — use Users/Me/OnboardingRequests?Direction=Received] Returns requests on projects the authenticated user has a role on, optionally filtered by project, user, and state. The 'state' filter and the response 'type'/'state' fields use stable PascalCase names (e.g. Pending, SelfOnboarding), not the legacy ints. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

post.description: [DEPRECATED — use Projects/{projectShortName}/OnboardingRequests] Creates a self-onboarding request to join a project as a member. Body {ProjectShortName, RequestType}. RequestType is the stable PascalCase name; only "SelfOnboarding" is accepted (422 with code request.unsupported_type otherwise, 400 for an unknown name). Returns 201; 404 (request.not_found / caller.not_provisioned) when the project or caller is unknown; 409 when already a member or a pending request exists. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

get.summary: List requests sent by the current user
get.description: [DEPRECATED — use Users/Me/OnboardingRequests?Direction=Sent] Returns requests submitted by the authenticated user, optionally filtered by state. The 'state' filter and the response 'type'/'state' fields use stable PascalCase names, not the legacy ints. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

get.summary: Get public request info for action link
get.description: Returns request details for an action link. No authentication required. On a failure read the 'code' extension for a machine-readable code (request.not_found, request.not_pending, request.expired, request.invalid_type); do not parse the message.

put.description: [DEPRECATED — use Projects/{projectShortName}/OnboardingRequests] Accepts a pending self-onboarding request and assigns the requester to the project as a member. Caller must hold a role on the request's project. Returns 204; 404 (request.not_found) when the request is unknown or outside the caller's scope — the two are deliberately indistinguishable; 409 when the request is already settled; 422 for non self-onboarding requests. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

[DEPRECATED — use Projects/{projectShortName}/OnboardingRequests] Rejects a pending self-onboarding request (terminal). Caller must hold a role on the request's project. Optional 'reason' query is accepted for parity but not persisted. Returns 204; 404 (request.not_found) when unknown or outside scope — the two are deliberately indistinguishable; 409 when already settled; 422 for non self-onboarding requests. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

post.description: Settles a self-onboarding request via a single-use action-link token. No authentication required. Using a link invalidates its siblings. Returns 200 when handled; 400 (code request.invalid_action_link) for an unknown, expired, or already-handled link. On a failure read the machine-readable code; do not parse the message.

Creates an onboarding request to join the route project as a member. The project is taken from the route; the request type is implicitly self-onboarding (no body). Any authenticated caller may create one (no project-scope check). Returns 201 with the GUID-free slug; 404 (onboarding_request.not_found / caller.not_provisioned) when the project or caller is unknown; 409 when already a member (onboarding_request.already_active_member) or a pending request exists (onboarding_request.duplicate_pending_request). On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

put.description: Accepts a pending onboarding request and assigns the requester to the route project as a member, atomically. Caller must hold a role on the route project. Returns 204; 404 (onboarding_request.not_found) when the request is unknown, outside the caller's scope, or belongs to a different project — the three are deliberately indistinguishable; 409 when the request is already settled. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

Rejects a pending onboarding request (terminal). Caller must hold a role on the route project. Returns 204; 404 (onboarding_request.not_found) when the request is unknown, outside the caller's scope, or belongs to a different project — the three are deliberately indistinguishable; 409 when the request is already settled. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

get.summary: List the onboarding requests the current user sent or can act on
get.description: Returns, as a paged list (?page=&limit=), the onboarding requests the authenticated user sent and the ones received on projects where the user is Owner or Manager. 'Direction' keeps one half: 'Sent' or 'Received', case-sensitive; without it both are returned. 'State' filters by state name and defaults to all states; send State=Pending for the requests still waiting. 'ProjectShortName' narrows both halves to one project. Each item carries the slug used to address it and a 'Direction' field ('Sent' or 'Received'); a request the user sent to a project they now manage is listed once, as 'Received', and as 'Sent' under Direction=Sent. The 'state' filter and the response 'state' field use stable PascalCase names (e.g. Pending, Accepted), not the legacy ints. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

get.summary: Get user info from access token
get.description: Returns LEXIS user info. Call on login to initialize/sync user.

get.summary: Get extended user info from access token
get.description: Returns extended LEXIS user info including project resources and HPC endpoint locations. Call on login alongside GetUserInfo.
Returns the authenticated user's JSON preferences, wrapped in a {"Preferences": {…}} envelope.

put.description: Replaces the authenticated user's JSON preferences (created on first write). The body is a {"Preferences": {…}} envelope, so a GET response can be sent back unchanged. Returns 204; 400 when "Preferences" is missing or null; 404 when the caller is unknown.

get.description: Returns all active locations, optionally filtered by provider name or by location type name (locationType, for example HPC; Unspecified matches nothing). Each location carries its LocationType as a name.

get.summary: Get location by provider and name
get.description: Returns a single active location addressed by its provider and name, with its LocationType as a name.
Returns all project tags, optionally filtered by name.
Returns a single project tag by its globally unique name.

Returns all valid request states as a bare array (a single complete page; X-Total-Count header, no Link). Each item carries the stable PascalCase Name (used in request/response contracts) and the legacy integer Id.

Returns all valid request types as a bare array (a single complete page; X-Total-Count header, no Link). Each item carries the stable PascalCase Name (used in request/response contracts) and the legacy integer Id.
Returns all valid operation mode identifiers and names.
Returns the valid location type names, without Unspecified.
Returns the names of all project domain types as a single complete page (bounded reference list — paging parameters are ignored). Use a returned name as the domainTypeName when updating a project.
Returns the valid allocation unit type names, without None. A name from this list is what AllocationUnitType takes on the assignment writes.

Returns the configured cluster authentication type names, the values PreferredAuthenticationType takes when creating a resource on a location. Whether a location's HEAppE instance offers a type is checked when the resource is provisioned.
Returns reference country data, optionally filtered by country code (substring match).
Returns platform-wide totals and weekly creation counts for projects, users and resources.

Returns the provider's resources that the caller can see (assigned to a project the caller has a role on), optionally filtered by project short name, location type name (locationType, for example HPC; Unspecified matches nothing) and validity dates. Each assignment carries its LocationType as a name.

get.summary: Get a provider's resource by name
get.description: Returns a single resource by its (provider, name) natural key if it is assigned to a project the caller has a role on; otherwise 404. Each assignment carries its LocationType as a name.

get.summary: Get the status of an async resource-creation request
get.description: Returns the flow status and per-step name/state summary for a resource-creation request submitted via the create-and-allocate endpoint (ADR-0057). Poll this URL — supplied as the 202 Accepted Location — until the flow reaches a terminal state (Completed or Failed). 404 when the request id is unknown.

put.description: Cancels a resource-assignment request by resuming whichever approval gate it is parked at with a cancel signal; the request terminates as Cancelled. Caller must hold a role on the route project. Returns 204; 404 (resource_request.not_found) when the request is unknown, outside the caller's scope, or belongs to a different project — the three are deliberately indistinguishable; 409 when the request is already terminal (resource_request.not_cancellable) or the workflow is not yet parked at its gate (resource_request.not_cancellable_yet, retryable). On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

post.summary: Re-send the PI approval link for a resource-assignment request
post.description: Regenerates the PI approval action link for a request still awaiting approval, invalidating the previous link, and re-emails the PI. Caller must hold a role on the route project. Returns 204; 404 (resource_request.not_found) when the request is unknown, outside the caller's scope, or belongs to a different project — the three are deliberately indistinguishable; 409 (resource_request.not_resendable) when the request is not awaiting PI approval. On a failure read the 'code' extension; do not parse the message.

get.description: Returns the resource request behind a single-use PI action-link token. No authentication required. Any unknown, expired, or already-used token returns an identical 404 (code resource_request.action_not_found) so token validity never leaks. Read the machine-readable code; do not parse the message.

post.summary: Settle a resource request via its action link
post.description: Delivers the PI's Approve/Reject decision (with an optional reason on reject) through a single-use action-link token. No authentication required. Returns 204 when the decision is accepted; an identical 404 (code resource_request.action_not_found) for any unknown, expired, already-used, or already-settled token; 400 (code resource_request.invalid_decision) for a decision other than Approve or Reject.

get.description: Returns the current application version. No authentication required.

post.summary: Request that a provider's resource be assigned to a project
post.description: Creates a project↔resource assignment request (ADR-0063). The caller must be an Owner or Manager of the route project (plan D10; out-of-scope is reported as 404 project.not_found, ADR-0018). Body {ProviderName, ResourceName, PrimaryInvestigatorEmail} names the resource and the PI to route approval to; the resource need not exist yet under that provider (it parks until created). Must not already be attached to the project (409 resource_request.already_attached), and must have no in-flight request for the same project/provider/resource (409 resource_request.duplicate_active). The provider is resolved within the caller's project scope, so one they cannot reach is reported as 404 provider.not_found, exactly like a missing one (ADR-0018). It must have a support e-mail (required to route requests for resources that do not yet exist; 422 resource_request.provider_no_support_email if missing). Starts the approval workflow asynchronously and returns 202 with the GUID-free slug and a Location header to the project's request list. On failure, read the 'code' extension, not the message. Status: 202 Accepted, 400 Bad Request, 404 project.not_found / provider.not_found, 409 resource_request.already_attached / resource_request.duplicate_active, 422 resource_request.provider_no_support_email, 502 resource_request.flow_start_failed (retryable).

get.summary: List resource-assignment requests on a project
get.description: Returns the resource-assignment requests raised on the specified project, optionally filtered by state, as a paged list (?page=&limit=). The caller must hold a role on the project (out-of-scope is reported as 404 project.not_found, ADR-0018). Each item carries the slug used to address the request's subsequent actions. The 'state' filter and the response 'state' field use stable PascalCase names (e.g. PendingPiApproval, Assigned). Status: 200 OK, 400 Bad Request (invalid state), 401 Unauthorized. On failure, read the 'code' extension, not the message.

get.summary: Get Cyclops usage for a project resource
get.description: Resource usage from the external Cyclops service. Served by the Gateway (authenticated and proxied to the Cyclops usage API); not implemented by Core, so it does not appear under api/v2.

200.description: Usage data returned by the Cyclops service.

400.description: ProjectShortName or ProviderResourceName is missing from the path.

403.description: The caller lacks permission to read usage for this project resource.

500.description: The Cyclops integration is not configured, or the Cyclops service could not be reached.

get.summary: Get aggregated Cyclops usage for a resource
get.description: Usage of a resource across all projects, aggregated by the external Cyclops service. Served by the Gateway (authenticated and proxied to the Cyclops aggregate usage API); not implemented by Core, so it does not appear under api/v2.

200.description: Usage data returned by the Cyclops service.

400.description: ProviderResourceName is missing from the path.

403.description: The caller lacks permission to read usage for this resource.

500.description: The Cyclops integration is not configured, or the Cyclops service could not be reached.
